A changed-risk lane (D-08-36) firing when internal/compiler/check's interprocedural summary/liveness code or internal/compiler/callgraph changes: it sweeps a synthetic call-graph corpus and re-fits the growth exponent gated by qlt02_budget_manifest.json's recomputed_work_growth_exponent row. Declared input gap: cache.DeclaredInputNames() has no name for the checker/callgraph package's OWN Go source (its seven names cover fixture text, build flags, toolchain identities, and translation units -- not the compiler's own source tree); go_toolchain is the closest available proxy, matching lane:qlt01-registry-audit's own precedent for a lane whose risk tracks the compiled harness rather than any one fixture. This is explicitly NOT the default edit loop -- a multi-shape size sweep exceeds what wiki/compiler-and-feedback-latency.md permits the default loop to pay; it runs at the mid-phase gate and pre-merge.

A changed-risk lane (Phase 09 Plan 06, D-09-28) firing when internal/compiler/corevalidate's loan-chain/endpoint-recomputation code (loanChainIndex/buildLoanChainIndex/carriedLoans/foldChain, corevalidate.go:1128-1238) or its Phase 09 peer-liveness derivation (corevalidate_peer_liveness.go: derivePeerLoanCarry/chainPeerLoanCarry) changes: it sweeps the same synthetic call-graph corpus (testsupport.GenerateCallGraphCorpus), post-processed with a genuine borrow injection so loan-carry propagation is actually exercised, and re-fits the growth exponent against corevalidate.Result.Checks, reported under peer_closure_recomputed_work_growth_exponent. This lane is DELIBERATELY DISJOINT from lane:interprocedural-cost-scaling above: that lane covers check's own bounded worklist fixpoint (buildInterproceduralSummaries/deriveFunctionUsesParam), a structurally different algorithm from corevalidate's one-shot reachability closure -- one of N independent peers' bound firing must never be read as covering the other peer's distinct cost curve (Key Lesson 3). Declared input gap and go_toolchain proxy choice mirror lane:interprocedural-cost-scaling's own precedent above, for the same reason (no cache.DeclaredInputNames() entry names a package's own Go source tree). Runs at the mid-phase gate and pre-merge, never the default edit loop.
